how-many-microgreen-trays-per-week.html.text:
Microgreens Tray Planner · GUIDE

How many microgreen trays per week?

Worked on invented numbers; replace them with yours in the planner.

The plan

Four crops, cut on Tuesday and Friday: 20 radish, 10 pea shoots, 15 sunflower and 10 broccoli trays a week. It sells about $881.36 a week, costs $178.55 in seed, media and packaging plus $90.00 fixed, and leaves $612.81, or $47.75 an hour for 12.8 hours of work.

Seeding days follow from harvest days

A 10-day crop cut on Tuesday is seeded on Saturday; cut on Friday it is seeded on Tuesday. Radish at 8 days is seeded on Monday and Thursday. Each crop's trays are split across your harvest days.

The rack is sized by the busiest day

WeekdayTrays on rack
Sunday73
Monday83
Tuesday65
Wednesday72
Thursday82
Friday55
Saturday65

The average is 70.7 trays a day, but 83 are on the rack at the peak. With 80 spaces the plan is 3 short on that day.

Rank crops by what a rack space earns

CropMargin per trayMargin per tray per day
Pea shoots$15.91$1.59
Radish$12.19$1.52
Sunflower$12.71$1.41
Broccoli$10.94$1.09

Pea shoots earns the most per rack-day and Broccoli the least, although Broccoli has the highest price per ounce. When the rack is the limit, rank by this column.

A small rack

With 40 rack spaces the best fitting mix on the defaults is 10, 16, 0, 0 trays of radish, pea shoots, sunflower and broccoli, making about $286.47 a week.

Common questions

How long does each microgreen crop stay on the rack?

The days from seeding to cut set how long a tray blocks a space. On the defaults radish takes 8 days, pea shoots 10, sunflower 9 and broccoli 10. A crop that takes a day longer holds every tray a day longer, which is why a slow crop needs more rack than its weekly tray count suggests.

Why does the rack need more spaces than the weekly average?

Because trays are seeded on some days and cut on others. On the defaults the average is 70.7 trays a day, but the busiest weekday holds 83. Plan for the peak, not the average.

Is this advice?

No. It is arithmetic on the numbers you type; check your local rules for selling produce.

Common questions

How many microgreen trays do I need to seed each week?

It depends on what you can sell and how long each crop sits on the rack. On the default numbers a plan of 55 trays a week (20 radish, 10 pea shoots, 15 sunflower and 10 broccoli) sells about $881.36 a week, but on the busiest weekday it holds 83 trays at once, so it needs 83 rack spaces. Enter your own crops, sales and rack size; the defaults are invented.

Which microgreen crop earns the most for the rack space it uses?

Not the one with the highest price per ounce. Margin per tray divided by days on the rack is what a rack space earns: on the defaults Pea shoots earns $1.59 per tray per day and Broccoli $1.09, even though Broccoli sells for the highest price per ounce.

What if I have fewer rack spaces than my orders need?

Fill the rack with the best-earning crops first, up to what you can sell. With a 40-tray rack the best fitting mix on the defaults is 10, 16, 0, 0 trays of radish, pea shoots, sunflower and broccoli and makes about $286.47 a week; the same plan on an 80-tray rack made $612.81.

Is this advice or market data?

No. It does arithmetic on the numbers you type. Prices, yields, days and costs are yours to check, nothing is uploaded, and it is not financial, tax, legal or food-safety advice. Check your local cottage-food, produce-safety and licensing rules before selling.
